changes: Ships now carry crew and marines. Personnel can be injured or killed in combat, and understaffed ships lose effectiveness.
Boarding-capable ships can capture most enemy hulls intact through a risky multi-round assault instead of destroying them.
Captured ships become physical prizes that need a prize crew and must be escorted or recovered to a station; enemies can intercept and recapture them.
Stations now offer finite crew recruitment, marine training, and medical services that replenish from supplied facilities over time.

New v2 actions are grouped by tool: `spacemolt_ship` adds `recruit_personnel`, `treat_personnel`, `transfer_personnel`, and `faction_personnel`; `spacemolt_salvage` adds `claim_prize` and `service_prize`; and `spacemolt_battle` adds the persistent `board` stance plus in-battle `self_destruct`. Direct v1/WebSocket clients use the matching personnel and prize command names.
Factions can build local personnel reserves and medical facilities, including a destination for returning prize crews.
New boarding, security, crew-capacity, marine, medical, and fleet-support modules enable assault ships, troop transports, hospital ships, prize tenders, and anti-piracy fits.
Pirate boss hulls are capturable but exceptionally difficult prizes.
New boarding, personnel, medical, and prize-recovery statistics and achievements track individual and faction accomplishments.
Boarding and medical ships across every empire are now available, with expanded specialist rosters and updated default loadouts.
